short: Negative Kähler curvature, no bounded chart

title.title: Negative Kähler curvature, no bounded holomorphic coordinates
title.subtitle: Claim: a contractible domain in $\mathbb C^3$ with pinched negative Kähler curvature that is not a bounded domain

plain: In one complex dimension, negative curvature forces a disc; in three, a negatively curved space can escape

beats.text: In one complex dimension such curvature forces the disc
Wu and Yau conjectured: contractible and pinched negative means a bounded domain
The claim: this domain has no bounded holomorphic coordinate system

steps: Build a Hartogs-type tube domain in three complex dimensions
Tune its Kähler potential so the curvature stays pinched negative
Yet every bounded holomorphic map degenerates somewhere

achievement.context: Before: compact negatively curved examples not covered by the ball (Mostow–Siu, Deraux)
achievement.note: The example still has two bounded coordinates; it lacks a full system

voice.text: In one complex dimension, pinched negative curvature forces the disc. What about higher?
A tube domain with a tuned potential stays negative, yet escapes every bound.
Claimed: contractible, negatively curved, yet not bounded.

sources.quote: There is a contractible Stein domain M in C^3 with a complete Kaehler metric with -B <= sec <= -A < 0, but no bounded holomorphic map M -> C^3 with nonvanishing Jacobian
Mostow-Siu and Deraux (compact negatively curved surfaces/threefolds not covered by the ball)
The example still has two bounded coordinates; the obstruction is to a full bounded coordinate system.
